newsitem.title: BULGARIA: BULGARIA DELAYS RULING ON ECONOMIC BANK INSOLVENCY.
newsitem.headline: BULGARIA DELAYS RULING ON ECONOMIC BANK INSOLVENCY.

text.p: The Sofia City Court on Tuesday postponed ruling on an insolvency case against state-owned Economic Bank, in receivership since September 23, for seven weeks, a court official said.

"The court postponed ruling for July 8 after bank sequestators demanded that its long-term assets be reassessed in line with the current (lev/dollar) exchange rate and inflation rate," the official told reporters.
Economic Bank sequestrators were not immediately available for comment.
The official said that reports on the bank's financial state prepared by three independent experts had been accepted by the court.
The Bulgarian National Bank (BNB) put Economic Bank in receivership on September 23 due to a danger of insolvency, citing a capital-to-risks assets ratio of minus 56.61 percent at end-August.
The BNB dismissed the bank's management and appointed sequestrators. The insolvency suit was filed five weeks later.
The BNB has sought insolvency through the courts for 16 state-owned and private banks or a third of Bulgaria's banks since May 17, 1996.
Four of them - the private Crystalbank, the Private Agricultural and Investment Bank, the private Trade and Savings bank and the state-owned Mineralbank have been declared bankrupt so far.
Consumer price inflation for April was 1,965 percent year-on-year. The lev traded near 1,600 to the dollar on Tuesday, compared to around 235 on September 23. -- Sofia Newsroom +359-2 911 88
